title: Make the cap door's registry import survive a vendored-lib-only fixture
action: dch-1 added a STATIC top-level import of queryRegistry/normalizeQueryPath from ../../../scripts/impact_registry.mjs into lib/cells.mjs. That breaks every fixture that vendors only .bee/bin/lib/*.mjs without a sibling scripts/ directory: packages/bee/hooks/test_write_guard.mjs's copyLib() builds exactly such a bare temp root, so the import throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, the hook's fail-open path swallows it, and SIX assertions in rows 5c/5d silently stop being checked. The suite reports failures nowhere near the real cause. dch-1's own verify (test_cells, test_cli_cells) never runs that file, so nothing caught it -- this is the same class of miss dch-1 exists to warn about, reproduced inside dch-1 itself. FIX: make the registry dependency lazy and failure-tolerant, so an absent module is the same silent skip E1 already requires for an absent or malformed registry. A dynamic import (or equivalent guarded resolution) inside the existing try/catch is the shape; a static top-level import of an out-of-tree module from a file that gets vendored alone is the defect. Also drop normalizeQueryPath if it is unused -- it currently is. E1's contract is unchanged: still a loud non-blocking warning naming the missing direct-edge suites when the registry IS reachable. Twin moves in the same commit.

truths: node packages/bee/tests/test_cells.mjs exits 0 with dch-1's warning tests still passing
Capping inside a bare vendored-lib fixture with no scripts/ directory neither throws nor warns
The warning still fires and names the missing suites when the registry is reachable

artifacts.substantive: registry dependency resolved lazily inside the guarded path

key_links: a missing impact_registry module is treated exactly like a missing registry file: silent skip
prohibitions: No static top-level import of an out-of-tree module from cells.mjs
No weakening of dch-1's warning when the registry is present

verify: node packages/bee/hooks/test_write_guard.mjs && node packages/bee/tests/test_cells.mjs && node packages/bee/tests/test_cli_cells.mjs

trace.outcome: Made the E1 impact-registry import lazy (await import inside the guarded try, capCell's lock callback made async) instead of a static top-level import; dropped the unused normalizeQueryPath import. A vendored-lib-only fixture with no sibling scripts/ dir now hits the same silent-skip catch as a missing/malformed registry file instead of crashing module load. Twins byte-identical.
